thread.title: Apple Hit by Weaker iPhone Sales Forecast - Barron's

author: Jon Swartz
title: Apple Hit by Weaker iPhone Sales Forecast - Barron's
text:
By Jon Swartz April 20, 2018 10:44 a.m. ET A Morgan Stanley forecast predicting weaker iPhone sales in the June quarter dinged shares of Apple (AAPL) Friday morning—but the firm also said that any drop in the company's stock when it reports results for that quarter could present a buying opportunity for investors.
iPhone X Illustration: courtesy of Apple Morgan Stanley lowered its estimate for iPhone unit shipments to 34 million from 40.5 million. ( Canaccord Genuity also lowered its June estimates, to 39.4 million from 43.7 million.)
"We expect Apple to report an in-line March quarter, but are cautious into earnings on May 1 due to our belief that June quarter consensus estimates need to be revised lower," analyst Katy Hulbert wrote in a research note to clients.
The note, entitled "Cautious Into the Print; Buy Any Post-Earnings Dip," offers more troubling fodder to an increasingly negative news cycle: The iPhone X isn't the top-seller Apple anticipated, the company is struggling to expand its supply of OLED screens, and demand for its products is weaker in China.
The company's success in China, where a potential trade war is brewing with the U.S., is considered crucial to keeping its profit margins intact.
Apple shares are down 3.4% in Friday morning trading to $166.90.
Despite the ominous report, Hulbert reiterated her overweight rating on Apple shares. She said investors should add to Apple positions in a postearnings stock decline. She did, however, lower her price target to $200 from $203.
"We would be buyers on any weakness following the print given 1) the Services story remains intact, (leading to a stronger and more consistent source of EPS growth and margin expansion), 2) estimate revisions are approaching trough (we already assume no device revenue growth next three years), and 3) buybacks remain a source of downside protection," she wrote.
